explanation: Kinematically allowed, not refused. eta photoproduction/electroproduction threshold in this code's Born kinematics (exclurad.F setcon: amhad(proton)=0.938272 GeV, amunm(eta)=0.54786 GeV) is W_thr = 1.486132 GeV. The requested W = 1.4885 GeV sits only ~2.4 MeV above threshold, giving a CM momentum for the eta/recoil proton of ~40 MeV/c (from the Kallen-function relation sqlw0/(2W) in bornkin) -- small but real and non-negative, so the kinematics are physical and the program will not hit a sqrt(negative) fault. Two threshold-proximity risks are flagged rather than blocking the run: (1) EtaMAID-2023 table grid in mpintp.inc has its first W node at 1.4856 GeV and its next at 1.500 GeV (14.4 MeV gap); the requested W=1.4885 GeV falls inside that gap, close to the lower edge, where the cross section is rising steeply from zero (threshold turn-on), so cubic-spline interpolation across only two widely-spaced table points may be less accurate than at higher W. (2) The natural radiative phase-space limit vmax = W^2 - m_eta^2 + m_p^2 - 2*W*m_p (bornkin) evaluates to only ~0.0026 GeV^2 here, far below the requested/default vcut=0.166 GeV^2, so vmax (not vcut) sets the effective inelasticity cut -- expected and not an error, but the radiative-tail integral runs over a very narrow interval near threshold, which can be numerically delicate. Used repo defaults for the remaining parameters: model=3 (maid2000/EtaMAID-2023), rc_mode=0 (full O(alpha) RC), bmom=6.535 GeV, tmom=0.0, lepton=1 (electron), ivec=1 (detected recoil proton), vcut=0.166 GeV^2 (CLAS12 analysis cut), matching the template input.dat and README conventions. No source-level correction was needed; the single-point input file input_eta_W1.4885_Q2_0.5.dat is ready to run as `./build/exclurad.exe < input_eta_W1.4885_Q2_0.5.dat`. Recommend the physicist sanity-check the output cross section/RC factor against a nearby, better-supported W point (e.g. W=1.500 GeV) to confirm the near-threshold interpolation is stable.
